headline: 2 Bangladesh police officers detained by BSF after crossing border
summary: An ASI and a constable from Brahmanpara police station were taken into custody by India's Border Security Force during an anti-drug operation.
details: Two Bangladeshi police officers, Assistant Sub-Inspector (ASI) Imran Hossain and Constable Rohit Dewan, were detained by India's Border Security Force (BSF) along the Comilla border.
The incident occurred around 10:30 PM on Thursday night near pillar 2059 of the Ashabari border in Shashidul Union, Brahmanpara Upazila.
The officers were conducting an anti-drug operation when a suspect attempted to flee. Constable Rohit Dewan chased the suspect and accidentally crossed the border into Indian territory.
After being detained by Indian citizens, ASI Imran Hossain was also taken into custody while attempting to rescue his colleague.
Local residents reported that the officers were beaten by some individuals linked to smuggling rings before being handed over to the BSF.
Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) is currently coordinating with the BSF to ensure the formal handover and return of the two officers to Bangladesh.
The Ashabari border area is known for smuggling activities and lacks a barbed-wire fence, making it easier for individuals to cross the border accidentally.

headline_marked: Over 200 named in case after [[man lynched over blasphemy allegations]] in Satkhira
headline: Over 200 named in case after man lynched over blasphemy allegations in Satkhira
summary: Wahiduzzaman Shamim was reportedly beaten to death in two separate attacks after a Facebook Live video called for a mob to gather against him.
details: A man named Wahiduzzaman Shamim (40) was lynched in the Kulia area of Debhata, Satkhira, following allegations of blasphemy. A murder case has been filed naming 10 specific individuals and 200 to 250 unidentified suspects.

Police officials stated that the prime accused, Fazlul Haque Amini, allegedly used Facebook Live to gather a crowd with the intent to kill Shamim. Amini remains at large, though operations to arrest the suspects are ongoing.
The attacks occurred in two stages on Tuesday, October 13. Shamim was first attacked while receiving treatment at a rural doctor's chamber after attempting suicide by consuming poison.
He was later attacked again at a hospital, where he eventually succumbed to his injuries. Local sources say the tension began after an audio recording of Shamim was circulated in the area.
The prime accused, Fazlul Haque Amini, claimed that Shamim had been making offensive remarks about Islam, Allah, and the Prophet (PBUH) for several days.

However, Shamim's brother, Sagar Sana, stated that Shamim was mentally ill due to family problems and often spoke abnormally. He argued that if a crime was committed, it should have been handled by the law rather than a mob.
